lessons.title: A Teacher's Story
lessons.description: A short passage about a dedicated teacher.

readingPassage.context: A short passage about a dedicated teacher.

paragraphs.native: ہمارے گاؤں میں ایک استاد رہتا تھا جو بچوں سے بہت محبت کرتا تھا۔
paragraphs.en: In our village lived a teacher who loved children very much.

paragraphs.native: جب بھی کوئی بچہ اسکول نہیں آتا تھا، وہ اس کے گھر جاتا تھا۔
paragraphs.en: Whenever a child did not come to school, he would go to their house.

paragraphs.native: اس نے کبھی ہمت نہیں چھوڑی، چاہے وقت کتنا ہی مشکل ہو۔
paragraphs.en: He never gave up courage, no matter how difficult the time was.

paragraphs.native: آج اس کے بہت سے شاگرد بڑے لوگ ہو چکے ہیں۔
paragraphs.en: Today many of his students have become important people.

paragraphs.native: جب بھی وہ اس استاد کو یاد کرتے ہیں تو ان کی آنکھوں میں خوشی آتی ہے۔
paragraphs.en: Whenever they remember that teacher, joy comes to their eyes.

lessons.title: The Law and the Common Good
lessons.description: A short passage on law, justice, and the common good.

readingPassage.context: A short passage on law, justice, and the common good.

paragraphs.native: قانون کا اصل مقصد ہر انسان کے حق کی حفاظت کرنا ہے۔
paragraphs.en: The real purpose of law is to protect every person's right.

paragraphs.native: جب قانون کمزوروں کی حفاظت کرتا ہے تو پورا معاشرہ مضبوط ہوتا ہے۔
paragraphs.en: When law protects the weak, the whole society becomes strong.

paragraphs.native: عدالتوں پر لوگوں کا اعتماد کسی بھی جمہوریت کی بنیاد ہے۔
paragraphs.en: People's trust in courts is the foundation of any democracy.

paragraphs.native: حکومت کی ذمہ داری ہے کہ وہ اداروں کو مضبوط بنائے اور انصاف قائم کرے۔
paragraphs.en: It is the government's responsibility to make institutions strong and establish justice.

paragraphs.native: جہاں انصاف ہو وہاں ترقی اپنا راستہ خود بناتی ہے۔
paragraphs.en: Where there is justice, progress makes its own way by itself.

exercises.question: What is the real purpose of law?
options: To punish everyone
To protect every person's right
To make money
To create fear

exercises.question: What happens when law protects the weak?
options: Society becomes weaker
The whole society becomes strong
Nothing changes
The economy fails

exercises.question: What is the foundation of any democracy, according to the passage?
options: Wealth
People's trust in courts
A large army
Fast transport

exercises.question: What is the government's responsibility, according to the passage?
options: To ignore institutions
To make institutions strong and establish justice
To close the courts
To avoid justice

lessons.title: Wisdom of the Ages
lessons.description: A capstone passage reflecting on wisdom, character, and civilization.

readingPassage.context: A capstone passage reflecting on wisdom, character, and civilization.

paragraphs.native: ہر تہذیب حکمت کی کچھ نشانیاں چھوڑتی ہے۔
paragraphs.en: Every civilization leaves behind some signs of wisdom.

paragraphs.native: جو قومیں اپنے کردار اور ضمیر کی قدر کرتی ہیں وہی صدیوں تک قائم رہتی ہیں۔
paragraphs.en: The nations that value their character and conscience are the ones that endure for centuries.

paragraphs.native: علم اور عاجزی مل کر انسان کو سچ میں عظیم بناتے ہیں۔
paragraphs.en: Knowledge and humility together truly make a person great.

paragraphs.native: کائنات کا نظام دیکھ کر ہمیں یاد آتا ہے کہ ہم اس دنیا کا ایک چھوٹا مگر اہم حصہ ہیں۔
paragraphs.en: Seeing the universe's system, we remember that we are a small but important part of this world.

paragraphs.native: اسی لیے ہر نئی نسل کو یہ حکمت آگے لے کر جانی چاہیے۔
paragraphs.en: That is why every new generation should carry this wisdom forward.

exercises.question: Which nations endure for centuries, according to the passage?
